news.title: India's commercial real estate investment rises 15% in 9M 2026: Report
news.para: In the first three quarters of 2026, India's commercial real estate investment rose by 15%, with cross-border investments hitting USD 5.5 billion, far surpassing mainland China. Grade A office yields between 7.75% and 8% are drawing investor interest. Data centers contributed significantly, reflecting positive overall market trends as the Asia Pacific region neared USD 200 billion in investments, underscoring strong activity.

news.title: Lucknow civic body offices to remain open on November 14 for property tax OTS applications
news.para: Lucknow Municipal Corporation's tax department will open on November 14 for applications under the one-time settlement scheme. Taxpayers may submit applications to recover outstanding property tax dues during this period. All zonal cash counters will also operate normally to facilitate the process. Additionally, Jal Kal department offices will remain open for revenue collection activities. Taxpayers can deposit amounts determined under the scheme until December 15, 2026.

news.title: Pune civic body expedites Holkarwadi town planning schemes amid push to aid ring road project
news.para: The Pune Municipal Corporation and district authorities are making strides in urban development, focusing on town planning in Holkarwadi to create a much-needed ring road aimed at reducing traffic congestion. Previous efforts in Uruli Devachi and Phursungi remain stalled due to administrative hurdles. To overcome these issues, a new arbitrator has been appointed to facilitate conversations with landowners.

news.title: Forest minister opposes Maharashtra government’s decision of cluster development in Navi Mumbai
news.para: Ganesh Naik has expressed strong opposition to the Urban Renewal Scheme in Navi Mumbai. He emphasizes the need for an impact assessment report before any redevelopment approvals. The Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation has also passed a resolution opposing cluster redevelopment without a citywide study. Concerns about population density and infrastructure strain have been raised by local leaders.

news.title: Bhubaneswar development body proposes extra floor area ratio incentive, new infrastructure fee
news.para: Bhubaneswar Development Authority plans to introduce incentives for landowners merging plots under town planning schemes. The proposed changes include a City Infrastructure Impact Fee for developments outside town planning areas. Incentives will include additional floor area ratio based on plot sizes after a deduction. A FAR Incentive Certificate will document the granted benefits and their usage. The draft regulations aim to streamline building and development processes while enhancing infrastructure.

news.title: CREDAI seeks major building regulation changes in Belagavi
news.para: Credai Belgaum has officially presented a memorandum to Buda to advocate for alterations in Belagavi's building regulations. The suggested modifications encompass a revision of building height classifications and setback standards for low-rise structures. Furthermore, Credai is urging the increase of floor area ratio for residential developments located on broader roadways.

news.title: Lucknow development body to roll out four new housing schemes
news.para: The Lucknow Development Authority will soon launch the 1.1-km Daliganj flyover, vital for enhancing transportation options. This project is integral to the Green Corridor effort, addressing severe traffic woes in the city. Alongside this, LDA is set to roll out four new residential schemes, providing housing opportunities for around 10 lakh residents in old Lucknow.

news.title: LIC Housing Finance ordered to pay over ₹2 lakh for CIBIL update failure
news.para: Veera Narender Reddy Y lodged a complaint against LIC Housing Finance for neglecting to update his CIBIL records post-divorce. Despite requesting the removal of his name as a co-applicant for the home loan, the company failed to notify CIBIL, adversely impacting his credit score. The commission deemed their service deficient and found them in violation of statutory obligations, awarding him compensation and ordering payment of litigation costs.

news.title: Maharashtra notifies new lift safety rules; monthly checks, annual audits now mandatory
news.para: Maharashtra will implement new lift safety regulations starting November 1, 2026, allowing a transition period of nine years for housing societies. These societies are required to upgrade their existing lift systems by October 28, 2027. Key components of the regulations include monthly servicing by certified contractors, annual safety audits, and the installation of safety features such as CCTV and automatic rescue devices.

news.title: Housing restrictions ease with government’s nod to Prayagraj master plan amendments
news.para: The Prayagraj Development Authority is set to revise the Prayagraj Master Plan-2031, easing construction limitations in pivotal areas. Residents and interested parties are invited to voice their objections and suggestions within a given timeframe. This initiative will enable the construction of residential buildings on smaller plots and allow for taller structures, facilitating the resurrection of delayed housing projects and expanding housing options in established neighborhoods.

news.title: Haryana RERA dismisses Joyville AOA plea, says registrar must decide upkeep handover row
news.para: A standoff between two residents' associations has postponed the management transition of the Joyville housing project. The Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority has rejected a grievance from the Joy Lavie Apartment Owners Association about the developer's control, stating that the legitimacy of the associations must be resolved by the Registrar of Societies.

news.title: Noida authority clears five facilities in sector-150 Sports City project
news.para: The Noida Authority has approved detailed maps for five sports facilities in the Sports City project. These facilities include a tennis centre, indoor multipurpose hall, swimming centre, and multipurpose playfield. Developers such as Prestige, County, Eldeco and Prateek are set to oversee the development. A cricket academy is already operational, adding to the sports infrastructure planned. Around 8,000 homebuyers have been anticipating this significant progress in the project.

news.title: Grasim Industries’ net profit declines 35% to ₹1,029.42 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: Grasim Industries recorded a 34.7 percent decline in net consolidated profit for Q2 FY27. The company's total income, however, increased by 25.3 percent in the same period. Revenue from the building materials business also saw growth, driven by improved profitability in cement. Additionally, Birla Opus and Birla Pivot both reported significant revenue increases in Q2 FY27. The company's investment in the Canadian joint venture further reflects its growth strategy.

news.title: TARC posts profit of ₹4.39 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: TARC Ltd has announced a consolidated net profit of Rs 4.39 crore for the quarter ended September. This is a significant improvement from a net loss of Rs 15.76 crore reported last year. Total income increased to Rs 134.06 crore from Rs 34.10 crore during the same period. The company achieved sales bookings of Rs 955 crore in the first half of this fiscal year.

news.title: Shriram Properties’ net profit jumps 152% to ₹21.59 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: In Q2 FY27, Shriram Properties posted a spectacular 151.9 percent growth in net profit compared to the last fiscal year, with total income climbing to ₹272.25 crore. The firm achieved record collections of ₹795 crore in the first half of FY27 and further solidified its position by acquiring more equity in four joint ventures, while ambitiously working to double its project portfolio.

news.title: Consumer commission orders Livspace to pay ₹87.16 lakh; cites unsafe work and inferior materials
news.para: Livspace India Pvt Ltd has been held responsible for unsafe renovation work in a Goregaon flat. The Maharashtra State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found the company guilty of poor workmanship and negligence. Deepak Ruiya, the complainant, reported serious safety hazards such as exposed live wires and a collapsing kitchen shutter. Following an incomplete project, the commission ordered Livspace to refund Rs 87 lakh to Ruiya.

news.title: Mumbai police order first eviction under Maharashtra Rent Control Act
news.para: City police have completed their first eviction under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, returning a flat to its owners. The owners claimed that tenants did not vacate their flat after their leave-and-licence agreement expired. The eviction proceedings were initiated, and the tenants were ordered to pay compensation for the delay. The government is addressing the backlog of rent-related cases in Mumbai with this new approach.

news.title: Godrej Properties acquires 31-acre land in Indore for plotted housing project
news.para: Godrej Properties has acquired around 31 acres of land for developing a residential project in Indore. The new project will offer a saleable area of approximately 0.7 million sq ft and contain various residential plots. This acquisition represents the company's third project in Indore, following the ongoing development of two existing projects.

news.title: West Bengal CM sets November 30 deadline for ineligible housing beneficiaries to return funds, orders CID probe
news.para: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has set a deadline of November 30 for ineligible beneficiaries to return funds as part of a crackdown on irregularities. This comes alongside a CID investigation into 57,000 potentially fictitious beneficiaries involved in a rural housing scheme. To ensure accountability, a special investigation team will oversee the process.

news.title: UP-RERA bars blanket consent from homebuyers for changes in building plans
news.para: Before making any significant changes to a project, promoters need to clearly inform buyers about how these changes will affect the carpet area, common areas, and overall project specifications in writing. Additionally, for any major alterations to the approved plans, they must get the written consent of at least two-thirds of the allottees involved.
